bar: Gate 1: OOS compounded return > 0 net of costs
Gate 2: per-period OOS profit factor >= 1.2 (RD-013's unit). The owner's standing removal rule applies to this PF: strict OOS PF < 1.2 => the cell is DELETE-class
Gate 3: >= 4/5 folds with positive compounded return

Gate 4 (the RD-013 drawdown gate, threshold unchanged): OOS max drawdown <= 20% — measured here on the DAILY close-to-close equity curve of the braked book with the running peak carried in from the full path. This is STRICTER than RD-013's period-granularity, reset-at-OOS measurement (daily drawdown is never smaller than period drawdown on the same path), so the comparison against the parent is conservative, not favourable
Gate 5: largest single-asset share of total positive P&L contribution <= 50% (contribution measured on the family's trade unit: per-asset sums of closed-episode net returns, OOS-entered)

Gate 6: one-sided t-test on OOS period returns, Bonferroni p < 0.05 / N_global under the frozen trial accounting below; a p within 2x of the threshold either way counts as FAILED (RD-013's fail-closed convention, i.e. passing requires p < alpha/2)
Gate 7: at 2x costs, compounded > 0 AND per-period PF >= 1.2

Gate 8 (trade-count): >= 200 closed OOS episodes AND episode PF >= 1.2. A cell with < 200 closed OOS episodes is judged 'insufficient OOS trades' — reported, never promoted, whatever the other gates say
A cell PASSES only if ALL eight gates hold. Near-misses are reported as texture, never promoted.

brake.execution: A scale change (or a rebalance) sets holdings to scale x current selection weights x equity at that close; the traded notional is charged exactly like a rebalance (see costs). While FLAT, weekly selections continue to be computed (they are the re-entry test) but no position is held.
brake.kind: Portfolio-level two-stage drawdown brake on the braked book's own equity. Single frozen parameter set — NOT a grid axis; it will not be varied, swept or re-tuned under this declaration. Any different brake is a new family under a new declaration.
brake.level_derivation: The levels are fractions of the programme's own 20% drawdown gate (level 1 at 1/2 of the gate, level 2 at 3/4, release at 1/4), chosen from the mandate's threshold — NOT fitted to RD-013's equity paths, which were never inspected for this design. Level 2 at -15% leaves 5 points of headroom to the 20% gate for gap-through between daily closes; whether that headroom suffices is part of what the run judges.

levels.level_1_trigger: DD(d) <= -10% while NORMAL => HALVED: exposure scale 0.5 from that close
levels.level_2_trigger: DD(d) <= -15% while NORMAL or HALVED => FLAT: exposure scale 0 (all cash) from that close
levels.release_from_flat: Evaluated only at a weekly rebalance close: if the fresh selection at that rebalance would be fully invested (all top-K scores > 0, i.e. selection weights sum to 1), re-enter at scale 0.5 (state HALVED, probationary) at that close; otherwise stay flat another week. From that HALVED state the ordinary rules govern (own-recovery release to NORMAL at DD >= -5%; re-flatten at DD <= -15%).
levels.release_from_halved: DD(d) >= -5% (the braked book's OWN drawdown recovery) => NORMAL: scale 1.0 from that close

brake.measurement: Close-to-close on the portfolio equity curve, computed causally. At each daily close d: signal equity = the book's mark at d BEFORE that close's trades; running peak = max of signal marks from the simulation start (2023-01-02, in-sample era included; the peak is never reset and the brake state path runs continuously across the IS/OOS boundary); DD(d) = signal equity / running peak - 1. Decisions at close d use only bars <= d and execute at close d (RD-013's trade-at-the-decision-close convention).
brake.no_volatility_targeting: There is NO volatility targeting of position sizes anywhere in this family — no vol estimate enters sizing at any point. RD-014's sizing mechanism is excluded by design, and FWD-006's forward-sizing ban on vol-targeting (for dow_effect) is respected in spirit: the brake is the family's only risk mechanism, as the mission specifies.

costs.mechanism: The RD-013 mechanism, extended to brake trades: at every trade event (weekly rebalance, brake trim, flatten, re-entry) the traded notional sum_i |w_new,i - w_current,i| is charged RT_i/2 per asset leg as an equity fraction and deducted at that close. The initial build from cash is charged. Cash earns 0. Turnover — including every brake whipsaw round trip — is therefore inside every judged number, including the drawdowns.
costs.x2_shadow: Gate 7 re-runs any cell passing the mechanical gates at 2x costs (RD-013's conditional pattern).

grid.cell_selection_disclosure: L in {63, 126} and K in {2, 3} are RD-013's two middle lookbacks and two broader breadths; L=21 (the parent's worst drawdowns, -57% to -60%) and L=252 (fewest independent bets) are excluded, and K=1 is excluded because gate 5 (single-asset share <= 50%) is structurally near-impossible at K=1 (parent's K=1 shares 0.51-0.66) and a one-asset book makes the rotation claim empty. This selection USES the parent's judged record and is declared as such; all 4 declared cells are counted in the global counter and judged whatever their outcome, and no cell will be dropped, added or re-parameterised after the run.
grid.control_record: The brake-off control for these exact cells is RD-013's judged record (weekly, long_flat): L63/K2 compounded +50.5%, DD -26.7%, period PF 1.33, folds 3/5; L63/K3 +54.7%, DD -21.0%, PF 1.38, folds 3/5; L126/K2 +17.9%, DD -32.6%, PF 1.17, folds 3/5; L126/K3 -4.4%, DD -37.2%, PF 1.06, folds 3/5. All four already fail gates besides the drawdown gate (folds 3/5 < 4/5; PF < 1.2 for both L126 cells). Declared plainly: the prior for this family is LOW — the brake addresses gate 4 only, and a PASS requires the braked book to also clear gates the unbraked cells failed. The family's value is a clean, counted verdict on the brake hypothesis for rotation; if it fails, the rotation-brake hypothesis is closed with it.

known_limitations_declared_upfront: Same-window judgement: the OOS window that judged RD-013 and informed RD-014 judges this family too. The cell selection and the release-rule design both derive from the parents' judged records on that window. The brake LEVELS do not (they are fractions of the 20% gate), and no parameter was fitted to any equity path — but a PASS here is weaker evidence than a pass on untouched data and would require forward (demo) confirmation before any promotion; a FAIL closes the rotation-brake hypothesis outright.

Probationary re-entry is a probe by construction: the book re-enters from FLAT at half scale while its drawdown against the all-time peak is still at the level-2 line, so a resumption that does not immediately follow through re-flattens within a day, at half-scale round-trip cost, and re-tests at the next Monday. This is the declared price of fast re-entry (RD-014's shadow-recovery release demonstrably paid more, in missed resumptions); turnover accounting charges every probe in full.

Daily-close brake granularity: the brake observes closes only. An intra-day crash through both levels is seen at the close; the 5-point headroom between the -15% trigger and the 20% gate is the only protection, and gap-through beyond the gate remains possible — gate 4 judges the outcome, not the intention.

Period-return accounting differs from RD-013 in one detail: costs enter through the post-cost equity base and period returns telescope exactly onto the daily equity curve, where RD-013 subtracted each rebalance's cost from the new period's return additively. Cross-terms are second-order; the control cells' SELECTIONS must still reproduce exactly (see verification_before_trust).

Gate 5's contribution is measured on episode net returns (the family's trade unit), where RD-013 measured it on period contributions. The threshold (<= 50%) is unchanged; the unit change is declared here, not smuggled.

Weekly cadence with K in {2,3} yields on the order of 122 OOS periods and a few hundred OOS episodes; if turnover is low, gate 8's 200-episode bar may be unreachable for some cells by construction. That outcome is a verdict ('insufficient OOS trades'), not a defect to be repaired by widening the grid after the fact.

The drawdown gate (max DD <= 20%) failed universally (best -21.0%, median about -35%, worst -60.3%); significance failed universally (best one-sided p = 5.9e-2 vs 2.5e-5 at N = 2,000); the four cells this family re-examines also failed folds (3/5 each) and mostly PF. This family changes exactly ONE thing — the book carries a portfolio-level drawdown brake — and re-judges under the same bar on the same OOS window. It is not a retune: RD-013's grid is not re-run, no RD-013 cell is re-judged, and the brake-off control is RD-013's existing judged record, not a new arm.
lineage_disclosure.boundary_vs_rd014: RD-014 (volatility-targeted trend with a drawdown brake) already tested A drawdown brake and failed 0/96 — on a different family on every axis: per-symbol trend signals (tsmom/EMA) on crypto30 at 4h/1d, volatility-target sizing in every cell (sigma* in {15%, 30%, 60%}), the brake as a grid axis {none, flat_05, flat_10, half_10} driven PER-SYMBOL by that symbol's unbraked shadow equity, judged per-episode through the rd2 machinery. This family has: a portfolio rotation signal (not per-symbol trend), RD-013's 7-asset cross-asset universe (not crypto30), NO volatility targeting anywhere, ONE frozen brake (not a brake grid axis, no brake-off arm), the brake driven at PORTFOLIO level by the BRAKED book's own equity (not per-symbol shadow equity), and portfolio period/DD judgement (not pooled per-symbol episodes). RD-014's closing mechanism note named the release rule as the suspect part of its brake — 'release on the braked book's own recovery or on fresh signal entry, not on shadow-equity recovery' — and this family's release rules are built to that named critique: HALVED releases on the braked book's own drawdown recovery; FLAT re-enters on fresh signal entry (the braked book's own recovery is mathematically impossible while flat, since a flat book's equity is frozen). This design debt to RD-014's judged post-mortem is declared, not hidden.
lineage_disclosure.mandate: TASK-STR-RD-013's board entry (VERIFIED 2026-11-15) records: 'If rotation is ever revisited it needs a risk mechanism (volatility targeting / drawdown brake) as a NEW pre-declared family, not a retune of this grid.' This family is that revisit, taking the drawdown-brake branch of the note. The volatility-targeting branch is NOT taken (see boundary_vs_rd014 and the no-vol-targeting rule below).
lineage_disclosure.what_is_new: Exactly one mechanism: a portfolio-level, two-stage drawdown brake (halve, then flatten) with own-recovery / fresh-signal release, applied to RD-013's rotation. Everything else — signal rule, universe, panel, window, folds, costs, bar — is inherited verbatim from RD-013 so the brake is the only changed variable.

prohibitions: Research only: no orders placed anywhere, no production code, registry or daemon changes, live trading prohibited. Demo/forward consideration only after a PASS plus forward confirmation, under separate governance. This declaration authorises exactly one run of the 4 declared cells; variants, re-runs with tweaks, or additional brake levels would each be additional trials under new declarations — none are authorised here.
question: Does RD-013's cross-asset momentum rotation, judged on the same panel, window and bar, survive its own drawdown gate when the book carries ONE pre-declared portfolio-level drawdown brake — and does it clear the rest of the programme bar the parent also failed?
sanity_checks: S1: frozen prices on all 7 assets => the book never invests (all scores 0, long_flat holds cash), equity constant at 1.0, zero episodes, zero brake transitions (synthetic test).

S2: truncation invariance — the simulation on a panel truncated at any date reproduces the full-panel equity path, brake transitions and closed episodes up to that date exactly (no look-ahead anywhere, brake included).

S3: turnover identity — a build from cash into 3 crypto assets at 1/3 each costs exactly 8 bps of equity; a later full exit costs exactly 8 bps more; period returns telescope onto the final equity to < 1e-9.
signal_rule: RD-013's rule verbatim. At each rebalance date t (weekly, Mondays): score = trailing L-calendar-day return (last close <= t vs last close <= t-L; each endpoint's bar within 3 calendar days of its target date; asset needs >= L+30 days of history, else ineligible at t). Hold the top-K at equal weight 1/K, mode long_flat: a selected asset with score <= 0 is held as cash, weight NOT redistributed. Fewer than K eligible: unfilled weight stays cash.
status: Frozen before any execution. No cell of this family has been run. This declaration, with its SHA-256, is posted on issue #35 before the runner is executed; the run additionally requires the coordinator's order.
title: Cross-asset momentum rotation with a pre-declared drawdown brake (RD-020)
trade_unit: One TRADE (episode) = one asset's continuous positive-weight run: opened when its weight leaves 0 at a trade close, closed when its weight returns to 0 (deselection at a rebalance, long_flat cash exclusion, or brake FLAT) or force-closed at 2026-11-01. Episode net return = the asset's compounded daily close-to-close return over the run x (1 - RT/2 entry drag) x (1 - RT/2 exit drag) - 1. Partial scale changes (brake halving, rebalances that keep the asset selected) do NOT open or close episodes. Episodes are counted unweighted by book weight (the RD-002 per-symbol counting convention).

trial_accounting.declared_at_arithmetic: Ledger: 3,885 executed trials (authoritative reconciliation 2026-11-16) + 4 STR-06 cells = 3,889, latest coordinator reconciliation 3,891. Minimum N_global for this family = 3,897; Bonferroni alpha <= 0.05 / 3897 = 1.2830e-05. If the ledger has risen by run time, the higher floor governs — the bar only tightens.
trial_accounting.method_frozen: The SRS frozen method: N_global = (programme ledger entering N, re-read at run time) + this family's trials — with one strengthening: this family charges itself for the two declared-but-unrun trials ahead of it in the queue (SRS 1, S-RD1 1) whether or not they execute first. N_global = max(ledger entering N at run time, 3893) + 4.
